corrections.form_value: Across 41.3 million natural-science papers (1980-2025), papers that use AI methods, mostly pre-generative machine learning, cover a 4.63% smaller median knowledge extent in SPECTER 2.0 embedding space than non-AI papers in all six disciplines (χ2 ≥ 84.05, p < 0.001; arXiv v4 p. 6, Fig. 3c), and their follow-on papers engage with each other 22.00% less (p. 6); the generative-AI-era subset is described as consistent but shown only in Supplementary Fig. S29 (p. 58).
corrections.source_says: The 4.63% is one figure for the median collective knowledge extent across science. Each of the six disciplines shows a contraction (χ2 ≥ 84.05, p < 0.001 in each), but v4 prints no percentage per discipline. As written, the sentence reads as a 4.63% contraction in every discipline. Suggested wording: 'a 4.63% smaller median collective knowledge extent across science, with a contraction in each of the six disciplines (χ2 ≥ 84.05, p < 0.001 in each)'.
corrections.quote: AI research is associated with a 4.63% contracted median collective knowledge extent across science, which is consistent across all six disciplines
corrections.locator: arXiv v4 p. 6, Results 'AI contracts science's focus'

corrections.form_value: Only the 2023-2025 subset of 4,797,614 papers bears on generative AI, and it is reported as figures only (Supplementary Figs S28-S30, pp. 57-59).
corrections.source_says: The subset is defined by publication date (the generative-AI era, 2023 on), not by use of generative AI. Inside it, 'AI-augmented' still means any AI method. Across disciplines, CNN and SVM rank first and second in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and LLM ranks 6th, 4th and 3rd. No analysis isolates papers that use generative AI. The reason should say this, because it matters for Review 1's scope decision.
corrections.quote: we replicated our findings with only the subset of papers published during the generative AI era
corrections.locator: p. 28, Supplementary Note 4.1; p. 70, Supplementary Table 5; p. 24, Supplementary Note 1.3

confirmed: Version: arXiv 2412.07727v4, dated 29 Nov 2025, 82 pages, headed '(Just accepted by Nature, to be online soon)'. Title and the four authors match (p. 1). The arXiv abstract page lists v1 10 Dec 2024, v2 4 Oct 2025, v3 18 Nov 2025, and v4 29 Nov 2025. candidates.json gives no arXiv id for c063.
Version of record: Nature 649(8099), 1237-1243, online 14 Jan 2026 (Crossref). OpenAlex lists it as closed access (oa_status 'closed'), so the form's 'closed access, not read' is accurate.
The Nature abstract (Europe PMC, PMID 41535462) prints the same headline numbers as v4: F1 0.875, 41.3 million papers, 4.63%, and 22% (v4 prints 22.00%).

Design is observational, and no study assigns people to AI. The only random steps are paper sampling and the random assignment of papers to expert annotators who validate the classifier (Extended Data Fig. 2, p. 14; Methods M4, p. 9). The design class and context class 'observational' are correct.

Corpus counts match: 41,298,433 papers (p. 1; Methods M1, p. 8), 310,957 AI-augmented papers or 0.75% (p. 2), 5,377,346 researchers (Fig. 1e, p. 3; Fig. 2b, p. 4), 2,282,029 career trajectories (p. 4; Methods M6, p. 10). The form records no people counts and puts corpus sizes in n_units, which is right for a corpus.
Eras: machine learning 1980-2014, deep learning 2015-2022, generative AI 2023 on (Methods M2, p. 8). Classifier F1 0.875 against expert labels (p. 2).

S1-O1 matches: 4.63% contracted median collective knowledge extent, χ2 ≥ 84.05, p < 0.001, df = 1, median test on any discipline (p. 6). Fig. 3c: p < 0.001, n = 1,000 samples in each field (p. 5). Contraction in more than 70% of over two hundred sub-fields (p. 6; Extended Data Fig. 9, p. 21). Knowledge extent is the maximum Euclidean distance to the centroid of 1,000-paper samples, repeated 1,000 times (Methods M8, p. 11).

S1-O2 matches: 'an lower entropy (χ2 ≥79.20, p < 0.001 and d f = 1 in median-test on any discipline)' (p. 6) and Fig. 3d, n = 1,000 samples in each field (p. 5). v4 prints no definition of knowledge entropy. The entropy is recomputed in PCA-reduced embedding space (Supplementary Fig. S34b, p. 63), so the code embedding_similarity fits.

S1-O3 matches: 4,797,614 generative-AI-era papers and the quote 'may appear less significant than corresponding results in our general findings' (Supplementary Note 4.1, p. 28). Fig. S29a prints n = 1,000 samples in each field and no test statistic (p. 58). Figs S28-S30 sit on pp. 57-59.

S1-O4 matches: 3.46% more expanded, t ≥ 1.91, p ≤ 0.1, df > 10^3 (the 3 is a superscript in the PDF), 30 out of 32 pairs (p. 6). Fig. 4a n = 27,405,011 (p. 7). Paper-family extent is measured from the focal paper (Methods M9, p. 11).
One-line finding: 22.00% less follow-on engagement (t ≥ 8.10, p < 0.001) is on p. 6. The generative-AI-era knowledge-extent replication is Supplementary Fig. S29 (p. 58).

Supplement holdings match: confound stratification Fig. S27 (p. 56), Web of Science replication Figs S31-S33 (pp. 60-62), distance robustness Figs S34-S37 (pp. 63-66), expert validation Tables S1-S4 (pp. 67-69). Extended Data Figs 1-10 sit on pp. 13-22.

The scope caveat that 'AI' here means mostly non-generative research methods holds. The paper says it is 'primarily covering decades involving development and deployment of conventional machine learning algorithms' (p. 2), and SVM, PCA, CNN and GAN lead the method rankings (p. 2; Supplementary Table 5, p. 70).

Code availability gives https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/AI-Impacts-Science (p. 82). The short form leaves data_and_code at its default, as the screener instructions allow. v4 has no funding or competing-interests statement, so company_involvement 'false' is consistent with the source.
summary: The form correctly classes c063 as observational context with no randomized study of people, and its version, corpus counts, and every reported statistic match arXiv v4 (pp. 1-11, 21, 28, 58) and the Nature record. Three wording fixes remain: the one-line finding applies the across-science 4.63% to each discipline, the reason's 'bears on generative AI' needs the caveat that the 2023-2025 subset is defined by date and is still led by CNNs and SVMs, and the supplement range should end at p. 77, not p. 82.
